newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Adsteam to float marine business.
newsitem.headline: Adsteam to float marine business.

text.p: The Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to sell its marine operations through a public float.

Adsteam said it would soon lodge a prospectus with the Australian Securities Commission, but gave no date for the planned float. The proposal was approved by shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting earlier this month.
Adsteam chief operating officer David Ryan said at the time that the company was well advanced with the float proposal and could proceed before June 30 if the opportunity arose.
Adsteam also said on Wednesday it would change its name to Residual Assco Group Ltd, to allow the floated marine operations to keep the name "Adsteam Marine".
Ryan has previously declined to comment on media reports that the sale of Adsteam Marine, Australia's largest marine towage operator, could raise up to A$160 million.
The joint underwriters of the float will be BZW Australia Ltd and SBC Warburg Australia Ltd.
Adsteam, one of Australia's largest corporate failures following the debt binge of the 1980s, came under the control of its bankers in 1990 with debts of A$11 billion.
This has been reduced to less than A$700 million with the float of former units such as Woolworths Ltd and David Jones Ltd. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
